video.title: Kubernetes Cluster Multitenancy Explained in 50 seconds! #vcluster

transcript.text: Imagine your company has five teams,
front end, back end, ML, QA, and DevOps.
All of them sharing the same Kubernetes
cluster to run their application. But
there's a problem. One team is using too
much CPU or power. Another team's pod is
talking to the wrong services. And then
security becomes a concern. What these
teams really need is a separate isolated
environment, fair resource sharing, and
secure access. And that's where
Kubernetes multi-tenency comes into
play. Multi-tenency means letting
multiple projects or teams use the same
cluster to run workloads keeping them
safe and separated. You can do this
using name spaces to separate workloads,
arbback to secure access, resource kas
to limit how much CPU and memory can be
used. But if you need more isolation,
you can also try out virtual clusters by
vclusters or dedicated clusters as well.
Subscribe.
